A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same survey, Personalized Generation In Large Model Era. Their text, three figures, and four appendix tables are readable and can be reliably matched across versions.

before.justification: v1 is a narrative survey without original empirical results. Tables 1–4 catalog cited methods, datasets, and metrics; experimental studies discussed in the text are attributed to other works.

after.justification: v2 remains a narrative survey. Its expanded literature discussion and appendix dataset entries introduce no original experiments, simulations, user studies, or empirical data analyses.

M1.justification: Section 2 retains the same personalized inputs, user-modeling components, and generative workflow. Newly described algorithms belong to cited research and do not constitute changes to a method proposed by this survey.

E1.justification: Table 2 adds HPD and U-sticker to the surveyed dataset catalog. Neither version actually uses these or other datasets for original training or evaluation, so experimental dataset and task coverage does not change.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates competing methods against a proposed algorithm. The additional methods in v2 participate in literature discussion, not baseline comparisons.

E3.justification: Neither version reports an original experimental protocol. The surveyed evaluation metrics in Tables 3–4 are retained; wording changes and the added SPL abbreviation do not change evaluation settings.

E4.justification: Neither version presents original ablations, sensitivity tests, robustness experiments, or empirical case studies. The additions to Section 5 discuss research challenges and possible approaches without testing them.

E5.justification: Repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, and other statistical uncertainty reporting are absent from both versions.

E6.justification: No experimental scores, rankings, or concrete empirical findings are added or revised. The appendix additions identify datasets, while the retained metric tables describe applicability rather than measured performance.

T1.justification: The conceptual task formulation, objectives, and workflow in Section 2 are retained. Neither version introduces mathematical assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims: a comprehensive cross-community survey, a unified user-centric framework, a multi-level taxonomy, and an overview of resources, applications, and open problems.

C2.justification: Section 5 adds filter-bubble risks and lifelong user-data management, identifies opportunities from unified multimodal models, and gives specific privacy and debiasing approaches. These extend the existing research outlook; the dedicated Limitations paragraph remains unchanged.

D1.justification: No implementation instructions, hyperparameters, hardware specifications, training costs, or code/data access instructions are added or revised. The new dataset entries provide names and citations rather than additional reproducibility information.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands the literature review across personalized audio, multimodal systems, and trustworthy generation. Additions include YourTTS, Voicebox, VALL-E X, PerFusion, R2P, CaT, and PVChat, alongside broader connections to privacy, debiasing, filter-bubble mitigation, and unified multimodal models.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized wording corrections, expands selected paragraphs, relocates the Plitsis et al. discussion to music generation, and adds acknowledgments and corresponding-author markings. The overall structure is retained, although the 3D metrics subsection becomes peer-level Section 3.5, shifting subsequent numbering.

P2.justification: All three illustrations and four table designs are retained. Table 2 expands two dataset cells with modest row reflow, Figure 3 shifts with pagination, and v2 removes page-number footers.

improvement.justification: Expanded audio and multimodal coverage, two additional dataset resources in Table 2, and concrete mitigation approaches in Section 5 make v2 more useful as a survey. The central synthesis and metric catalogs remain largely unchanged, making the overall gain incremental. These benefits outweigh the small heading-hierarchy regression introduced by making 3D evaluation metrics Section 3.5.
